nodes.rationale: B1 can move the public main in remote step 4, and M1 to M5 are guards or remote-proof steps that pass or misbehave where the spec intends otherwise

nodes.label: Verdict of the second review at ee8e750: Approve with nits
nodes.rationale: No blocker or major finding open; B1 and M1 to M5 closed; fifteen new minor findings, none can harm the remote

nodes.label: Second review, fix round at ee8e750 (range 9e03aa7..ee8e750, 16 files)
The new Remote proof, step by step: no command can leave the remote in an unintended state
Nits of the second round (linux-build fatal line wording, git status -sb, placeholders, C3 messages, secrets case, trap without exit, stale sbom file, ...)
Before the remote steps: m3, r2-m1, r2-m3, r2-m4, in order of weight
nodes.rationale: No finding blocks the remote proof; these four are small and worth doing first; r2-m6 and r2-m7 can go into the closing pull request

nodes.label: What is good in the fix round: bounded waits, C3 as allowed list, M5 fixed at the root, Gap tests turned to refusals, no regression
Summary of the first pass: seven required checks behind scripts/check.sh, guards that pass while the protected thing is broken
B1 (blocker): remote step 4 may be accepted by GitHub and move main
nodes.rationale: State: closed. The pushed commit was the green head of an open pull request with 0 approvals, so GitHub could accept the direct push; fixed by an empty commit-tree probe on origin/main with a gate on rule types and names

nodes.label: M1 (major): the branch rule goes live before any check has run on a GitHub runner
nodes.rationale: State: closed. A first run on a new runner often fails for reasons outside the code; fixed by reordering so the rule is applied in step 3 after seven passes

nodes.label: M2 (major): the steps after the merge are not written down
nodes.rationale: State: closed. AC-3 evidence could reach main only through a second pull request; fixed by remote step 7, the closing pull request

nodes.label: M3 (major): rule W5 misses a forbidden dependency in four ordinary TOML spellings
nodes.rationale: State: closed. Header with comment, quoted key, per-dependency target table and package rename passed; W5 is the only automatic guard for core/control independence

nodes.label: M4 (major): a required check can be switched off and pool-repo-check ci still passes
nodes.rationale: State: closed. continue-on-error, if:, shell:, container:, env: and continuation lines were not read by C3; fixed by making C3 an allowed list of keys

nodes.label: M5 (major): rule D6 passes when the base revision cannot be read
nodes.rationale: State: closed. A failed git show was treated as an absent file, so D6 reported ok without comparing; roads 2 and 3 closed by 0e68e2a, road 1 by keeping absent and unreadable apart

nodes.label: m1 (minor): three remote proof commands will not show what Expected says (gh pr checks --watch, git branch -D, unfinished push run)
nodes.rationale: State: closed. They fail without harm but stop a set -e block early

nodes.label: m2 (minor): the undo paragraph understates what changed on the remote
nodes.rationale: State: closed. It omits the merge commit and the remaining scope branch, and $R is unset in a new shell

nodes.label: m3 (minor): the evidence is older than the tree that will be pushed
nodes.rationale: State: open, in work (closed later by the verify after the review fixes). verify.md ran on f58885f/535bd15 before ae6a77b and 0e68e2a; no prove-checks run covers the pushed tree

nodes.label: m4 (minor): stale sentence 'added below when the build is done' in the technology evaluation
nodes.rationale: State: closed. The observed versions have been added

nodes.label: m5 (minor): the unsafe rule is stated with no exception in engineering standards
nodes.rationale: State: closed. The fuzz package is the one place where unsafe_code does not apply

nodes.label: m6 (minor): the agent guides are behind the tree (AGENTS.md says no CI and nothing beyond scope 001)
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose (left to the sync step and the closing pull request). Once the rule is active an agent following the guide would plan a direct push

nodes.label: m7 (minor): a failing git is not noticed in scripts/linux-build.sh
nodes.rationale: State: closed. git status failure counts as clean and git archive runs without pipefail; exit 1 where the contract says 3

nodes.label: m8 (minor): check_sbom leaves files in the tree when the tool fails
nodes.rationale: State: closed. A leftover pool.cdx.json makes linux-build exit 3 with no hint

nodes.label: m9 (minor): an exported CDPATH or GIT_DIR sends the scripts elsewhere
nodes.rationale: State: closed in part (r2-m13 left). prove-checks.sh promises never to change the tree it started from; GIT_DIR could land case 20's commit in the source repo

nodes.label: m10 (minor): unsound advisories on indirect dependencies do not fail deny
nodes.rationale: State: closed. cargo-deny 0.20.2 defaults unsound to workspace; the spec wants direct and indirect alike

nodes.label: m11 (minor): half of the dependency policy has no proving case
nodes.rationale: State: closed as scoped. A later edit that weakens sources or bans would pass every check, against the purpose of AC-11

nodes.label: m12 (minor): the --base value reached git as an option
nodes.rationale: State: closed. Safe by luck; closed by 0e68e2a with --end-of-options

nodes.label: m13 (minor): a comment in a manifest gives a false alarm or a wrong message (W4)
nodes.rationale: State: closed. Fails closed but blocks honest edits

nodes.label: m14 (minor): W4 checks only the members written in the members array
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. Path-dependency members escape unsafe_code = forbid; W1 still shows the name

nodes.label: m15 (minor): W3 has three quiet ways around it (target folders, grouped imports, symlinked .rs)
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. The grouped import is an everyday spelling

nodes.label: m16 (minor): C5 accepts more permissions after a blank line or a comment
nodes.rationale: State: closed in part (r2-m6 left). nothing_more looks only one line ahead

nodes.label: m17 (minor): the CI guards do not require the fixed shape they rely on
nodes.rationale: State: closed in part, as the spec now says. Second workflow file, secrets index form, quoted keys, job name:, on: block and main.json fields pass

nodes.label: m18 (minor): symbolic links are skipped without a message
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. Linked files escape W3, W6 and D1-D5

nodes.label: m19 (minor): the Markdown reader differs from GitHub in a few places
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. Committed documents use none of these forms

nodes.label: m20 (minor): the scripts/check.sh tests never assert which commands a check runs
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. Empty check bodies would still pass the suite

nodes.label: m21 (minor): entry point paths with no automated test (linux-build, tools, fuzz, sbom, origin/main fallback)
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. These branches decide between exit 1 and 3; m7 and m8 sit there

nodes.label: m22 (minor): nine tests pin a hole as the expected result, marked only by a comment
nodes.rationale: State: closed in the main. A pinned defect that looks like a passing test tends to become the rule

nodes.label: m23 (minor): smaller gaps in the test suite
nodes.rationale: State: open, on purpose. Substring matches that do not prove the claim, a silent skip, tests reading the working tree

nodes.label: r2-m1 (minor, second round): the condition before step 1 cannot be met word for word
nodes.rationale: State: closed in substance by the remote evidence record (diff between checked and pushed revisions). Recording the revision is a commit, so the pushed revision always differs; unclear text, not a risk

nodes.label: r2-m2 (minor, second round): the probe gate does not look at the bypass list
nodes.rationale: State: open. If main.json ever carried a bypass actor the probe would land on main; not live today

nodes.label: r2-m3 (minor, second round): an empty PROBE or BEFORE turns a push into a delete request
nodes.rationale: State: open. AC-13 could be recorded as passed by mistake although the remote stays safe

nodes.label: r2-m4 (minor, second round): the cleanup of step 4 offers the forced push first
nodes.rationale: State: open. A forced push to a public default branch is the riskier act; leaving the empty commit breaks nothing

nodes.label: r2-m5 (minor, second round): verify.md still uses the old step numbers
nodes.rationale: State: closed by the Remote step numbers table of the verify after the review fixes. Pending rows mapped AC-3, AC-5 and AC-13 to old step numbers and said 21 proof cases

nodes.label: r2-m6 (minor, second round): C5 still accepts a permission after a comment in the first column
nodes.rationale: State: open. YAML reads two permissions while the guard says ok; the m16 comment input

nodes.label: r2-m7 (minor, second round): nothing before jobs: is held, and the spec does not list that
nodes.rationale: State: open. A workflow level defaults: run/shell or a changed POOL_CHECK_BASE pass and can neutralise checks or D6

nodes.label: r2-m8 (minor, second round): C3 reads keys without their place
nodes.rationale: State: open. run: under with:, - run: in a text block, a flow-style job and a lone carriage return pass; all need intent

nodes.label: r2-m9 (minor, second round): W5 still misses four rare spellings
nodes.rationale: State: open. Follow-up 10 holds the decision to read edges from Cargo.lock before a third crate

nodes.label: r2-m10 (minor, second round): a member written in single quotes is not checked at all
nodes.rationale: State: open. Should be fixed before the slice that adds a third crate

nodes.label: r2-m11 (minor, second round): two additions to W5 are right but not in the spec, and one is applied too widely
nodes.rationale: State: open. The root rename is applied without workspace = true, giving a false alarm

nodes.label: r2-m12 (minor, second round): closed holes that no test holds closed
nodes.rationale: State: open. The HEAD:docs fix of M5 can be undone with no red test

nodes.label: r2-m13 (minor, second round): check.sh fuzz still follows an exported CDPATH
nodes.rationale: State: closed by 8cfb720 (CDPATH= cd -- crates/pool-config). fuzz is not a required check, so CI is not affected

nodes.label: r2-m14 (minor, second round): proof case 22 leaves a clone in the Cargo home on every run
nodes.rationale: State: open. No build is affected; ~/.cargo/git only grows

nodes.label: r2-m15 (minor, second round): unsound = "all" has no proving case and is not on the list of unproven parts
nodes.rationale: State: open (the verify after the review fixes probed it by hand). Case 6 uses a vulnerability advisory, not an unsound one
